_README: EVERY price constant in this experiment lives in this file, and nothing else in the
repo contains a currency figure. scripts/cost.py is a pure function of
(measured resources from results/raw) x (these constants). Change a number here and
re-run `python3 scripts/cost.py` to get new dollars from the SAME measurement --
COST IN THIS REPO IS MODELLED, NOT BILLED. No cloud account was charged. The
measured quantities are CPU-seconds, wall seconds, peak RSS, request count and
cold-start latency; the dollars are those quantities multiplied by these constants.
how_read: Pulled from the AWS Price List Bulk API, us-east-1 region files, on the date above.
These are public, unauthenticated JSON/CSV endpoints, so every figure below is
reproducible with curl and jq rather than transcribed from a marketing page.
The effectiveDate stamped inside the fetched files was 2026-08-24.

_note: The shape ENFORCED on the container in docker-compose.yml, identically on both
arms, and the shape the model bills. Enforced and billed are deliberately the
same object: costing a reservation that was not enforced would price latency
produced by resources nobody paid for.
Emulated-platform parameters, not prices. idle_timeout_s is how long a
scale-to-zero platform keeps an instance warm after the last request before
stopping it -- the single knob that decides whether an idle gap costs you
money or costs you a cold start. It is declared here and enforced by
scripts/run.sh, which really does stop the container when the gap exceeds it.

lambda_arm.label: Lambda ARM (GB-second + per-request)
source_lines: billed_gib_override: Lambda has no separate vCPU price -- CPU is allocated in
proportion to configured memory, and ~1 vCPU arrives at 1769 MB. To buy the
1 vCPU this experiment reserved you must configure 1769 MB = 1.7275 GiB, so
that, not the 512 MiB actually touched, is what Lambda bills.
Free tier (400,000 GB-s, 1M requests) is NOT applied: it is a fixed monthly
credit, so including it would make the answer depend on total account usage

ec2_m7g_large_packed.label: EC2 m7g.large on-demand, packed
source_lines: $0.0816 per On Demand Linux m7g.large Instance Hour (2 vCPU, 8 GiB, Graviton3)
Cost is attributed as the LARGEST fraction of the instance the reserved shape
occupies on either axis, i.e. max(vcpu/2, gib/8). That charges for the
binding dimension and assumes the rest of the node is perfectly filled by
other work -- the most charitable possible assumption for the always-on arm.

_note: Charged per CLUSTER, not per workload, so the headline numbers EXCLUDE it --
the charitable reading for the always-on arm, which assumes the cluster is
already paid for by other services. cost.py reports a separate sensitivity
row showing what it does to a single-service cluster, because for one
workload it dwarfs the compute.

same_rates_isolates_idle.label: Same rates on both arms - isolates idle time
_note: The controlled comparison. Identical unit prices on both arms, so the only
thing left to move the dollars is billed seconds -- i.e. idle. Any crossover
here is caused by idle and cold starts and nothing else.

typical_shapes.label: Lambda vs an EC2-backed node - what people actually compare
_note: The uncontrolled comparison people actually make. It mixes TWO variables:
billed seconds and unit price. Reported second, and never as the
explanation for the first.
